c_armedGated.summaryLineHonesty: The charter anticipated a summary line reading '7 passed, 1 expected failure, 0 unexpected passes'. Playwright's list reporter does not print that sentence: it prints the aggregate '8 passed' and marks the expected-failure row 'x' while the seven genuine passes are marked 'ok'. This is the same accounting the rewind-pack precedent produced ('6 passed ... as six expected failures'). The decomposition recorded above - 7 ok, 1 x, 0 unexpected passes - is read off the per-row reporter lines, not inferred from the aggregate.

whatTheGateDoesAndDoesNot.does: Converts a row that reaches a measured product refusal into a declared expected failure, so the group is green today and turns RED the day the refusal disappears (an unexpected pass is reported as a failure).
whatTheGateDoesAndDoesNot.doesNot: It proves nothing about E2E-25's letter. The redaction clause - 'player views SHALL show the authorized result while only the GM private record contains the private detail' - is NOT discharged by this unit.
whatE2E25StillProvesBeforeTheRefusal: The private reason reaches the server: expect(committed.request().postDataJSON().reason).toBe(reason) is the line immediately above the refusing assertion and it passes.

The correction lease admits the named head, digest and generation: candidate-verification-failed is raised downstream of the lease acquisition, so the 64-hex expectedDigest guard let the request through.
whatTheGateDoesAndDoesNot.whyThisIsNowAllowedWhenU2bSaidItWasNot: U2b's header forbade the mark because U2b's scope was to make BOTH rows green and a gate would have hidden its own failure. U2c's scope, written by the parent after U2b parked, is explicitly the gated shape under council decision 7: the gated set is exactly the authored rows carrying a strict test.fail with a named gate tag. U2c replaces that header paragraph rather than contradicting it silently.
